editorial_thesis: Today’s strongest signal is the move from agent demos toward governed work surfaces: native IDE participation, disposable data planes, reproducible evidence, and human checkpoints in consequential workflows.

topic_groups.title: Agent-Ready Developer Surfaces
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Two fresh IDE integrations show coding agents becoming interchangeable participants in native developer environments, while the key differentiator is now isolation and review rather than autocomplete.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot in Xcode’s coding assistant
sources.why_selected: Native integration reduces context switching and makes the agent part of the same review surface as the project, not a separate chat window.
sources.usefulness: Use it to test a mobile-client workflow where the agent must edit, build, and explain changes inside the existing IDE boundary.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot in JetBrains Air
sources.why_selected: Parallel sessions, cloud execution, and in-context review turn coding delegation into a repeatable work queue rather than a one-off prompt.
sources.usefulness: Prototype a Buildn repair queue with one task per fresh sandbox, repository-scoped context, and a patch review gate.

sources.title: Agent Client Protocol
sources.why_selected: A client protocol makes the host environment less dependent on a single agent vendor and supports replaceable execution backends.
sources.usefulness: Treat ACP-like boundaries as a design reference for Buildn surfaces that need interchangeable workers with shared evidence contracts.

sources.title: Physical-Engineering’s Last Exam
sources.why_selected: Agent evaluation is expanding from coding and QA into professional workflows where constraints, calculations, and domain artifacts matter.
sources.usefulness: Borrow the benchmark shape for Buildn client tasks: score artifact correctness, constraint satisfaction, evidence, and review effort.

topic_groups.title: Agent Runtime + Data Plane
topic_groups.selection_rationale: This lane earns inclusion because the newest practical releases connect agent execution to isolated desktops and disposable, policy-bound databases—two missing pieces in many prototypes.

sources.title: WorkSpaces for AI agents: Linux and Windows 11
sources.why_selected: Agents can work in the same OS-specific environments as people, including legacy Windows applications and Linux build tooling.
sources.usefulness: Evaluate it for client workflows that cannot be cleanly re-platformed but still need isolated, auditable computer use.

sources.title: AlloyDB Express
sources.why_selected: Coding agents can create isolated test data planes quickly without making every prototype a long-lived infrastructure project.
sources.usefulness: Spin up per-job databases for Buildn experiments, store structured evidence beside vectors, and destroy or retain them by policy.

sources.title: Agent Compute Engine and expanded governance
sources.why_selected: It makes waiting, resuming, egress, and per-agent identity first-class runtime concerns instead of hidden application code.
sources.usefulness: Use the design as a checklist for Buildn job isolation even when implementation stays local or Kubernetes-based.

sources.title: Step Functions as agent tools
sources.why_selected: It separates model judgment from business-process execution and keeps approvals, retries, and state transitions explicit.
sources.usefulness: Wrap client onboarding, report generation, or publishing flows as typed tools rather than giving an agent broad API access.

topic_groups.title: Evidence-Bearing Science + Evaluation
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fresh releases from Anthropic and OpenAI point to a common pattern: agents become useful in complex domains when outputs carry executable artifacts, provenance, and a human checkpoint.

sources.title: Claude Science
sources.why_selected: The product treats code, environment, explanation, and message history as part of the result rather than incidental implementation detail.
sources.usefulness: Mirror the artifact contract for Buildn research: claim, source, code or query, environment, reviewer notes, and next action.

sources.title: Accelerating engineering for the physical world
sources.why_selected: It shows the agent opportunity moving from text generation to coordinated artifact transformation across constrained engineering systems.
sources.usefulness: Look for client workflows where repeated consistency checks across documents, drawings, and specifications can be automated first.

sources.title: LifeVal
sources.why_selected: It measures whether an assistant actually completes useful workflows, including research, decisions, browser use, and user checkpoints.
sources.usefulness: Use the task-based framing to replace vague “helpfulness” claims with accepted outcomes and explicit escalation points.

sources.title: Thousands of agents analyze whole-brain CRISPR data
sources.why_selected: The durable pattern is partitioned investigation over structured data with shared schemas, intermediate evidence, and a final triage step.
sources.usefulness: Adapt it to repository archaeology, competitive research, or client discovery with claim-source-confidence-next-test records.

topic_groups.title: Personal + Physical Workflows
topic_groups.selection_rationale: This is a deliberate coverage-gap lane: recent dossiers emphasized infrastructure, while current signals show agents moving into everyday assistance and physical-system design where trust, consent, and review are decisive.

sources.title: How agents are transforming work
sources.why_selected: The relevant unit of adoption is a task with a time horizon, tools, and an accountable owner—not the number of prompts or generated tokens.
sources.usefulness: Frame Buildn/client discovery around delegated work units: duration, acceptance criteria, review cost, and escalation.

sources.title: Claude Science local and HPC workflow
sources.why_selected: The pattern joins local-first data residency with agentic orchestration instead of forcing every dataset into a hosted workspace.
sources.usefulness: Study it for privacy-sensitive client analysis where evidence can stay on the client’s infrastructure while the agent receives narrow context.

sources.title: GPT-Rosalind biological reasoning model
sources.why_selected: Its operational value is inseparable from orchestration, grounding, and hypothesis triage; a model name alone is not a workflow.
sources.usefulness: Use it as a reminder to evaluate model-plus-data-plus-review systems rather than isolated benchmark scores.

sources.title: Agent Compute Engine’s pause/resume pattern
sources.why_selected: Human checkpoints become economically viable when waiting does not consume a continuously running process.
sources.usefulness: Design approval-heavy Buildn workflows that pause after producing a proposed change and resume only after an explicit decision.
